cards.subject: math

objective.text: Split a whole into equal parts. Name the fractional unit. Count the unit fractions.

explanations.title: Equal parts
explanations.text: A whole can be split into equal parts. Equal parts are the same size. 2 equal parts are halves. 4 equal parts are fourths. 3 equal parts are thirds. 6 equal parts are sixths.

explanations.title: Name the unit
explanations.text: The name of the fractional unit comes from the number of equal parts. 1 of the 2 equal parts is 1 half. Count the parts: 1 half, 2 halves.

explanations.title: How to know parts are equal
explanations.text: Fold the strip. The sides match perfectly. Or measure each part. A 12 inch strip split in 2 has two parts of 6 inches. 6 plus 6 is 12.

explanations.title: More parts, smaller parts
explanations.text: The whole stays the same. When you split it into more parts, each part is smaller.

objective.text: Explain equivalence by manipulating units and reasoning about their size.

explanations.title: More parts, smaller parts
explanations.text: When you cut a whole into more parts, each part is smaller. The number of parts gets larger.

explanations.title: Same shaded area
explanations.text: Equivalent fractions cover the same area. The parts change, but the shaded area does not.

explanations.title: Double or triple the units
explanations.text: Cut each part in 2 to double the parts. Cut each part in 3 to triple them. The whole stays the same.
